subject: QBR: Infra fallback & unit-economics plays (capacity, GPU spend, batching/cache tradeoffs)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01 18:05 PDT
Subject: QBR: infra fallback & unit-econ plays (capacity, GPU spend, batching/cache tradeoffs)

Team —

I want to consolidate the QBR asks for infra capacity and a short list of fallback plays we can present to execs. We're laser-focused on two things for the deck: (1) runway (how many weeks of predictable capacity at current growth) and (2) unit economics levers we can push in the next 4–8 weeks without significant engineering lift.

Current snapshot (pulled last week):
- Total monthly GPU spend (hosted + dedicated): ~$1.18M/mo
- Cluster average utilization: ~58% (p90 request latency SLOs observed)
- Effective tokens/second per GPU varies heavily by model family; tail loads increase per-token cost by ~20–30% when KV cache misses spike

Suggested fallback plays (short bullets we can show):
1) Dynamic model-tiering: route non-latency-critical requests to cheaper quantized variants (saves ~25–40% per-token depending on model).
2) Slot-bursting + pre-warm windows for expected traffic peaks (keep cold-starts under control).
3) Aggressive prefix/KV caching for chat-heavy customers (we've measured 12–18% unit-cost improvement on average).
4) Short-term batch-size nudges for background jobs (increase batching for async workloads, ~10–15% token cost reduction).
5) Manual burst credits for 2 top enterprise customers while we finalize Dedicated capacity (cost vs. SLA tradeoff).

Asks:
- Karthik: can you validate the GPU spend number and pull a conservative worst-case scenario (growth + 20% week-over-week for 6 weeks)? Attach model-level cost rows.
- Lauren: please add an exec-slide for risk (latency/regression) and a single-line recommendation on whether we should push temporary price-protection credits for top customers.
- Marissa: I need a 1-page appendix with quick Win/Lift estimates for each play (engineering weeks, expected % cost delta).

I've attached a working spreadsheet (qbr_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) and a 1-page unit-econ summary PDF. Use those as the source of truth and update with your conservative figures.

Goal: have a 6‑slide summary + 1 appendix by EOD Friday so we can sync with finance early next week.

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Infrastructure & Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01 20:30 PDT
Subject: Re: QBR: infra fallback & unit-econ plays (capacity, GPU spend, batching/cache tradeoffs)

Rishi —

Quick pass: numbers look broadly right. I'm attaching the model-level breakout inside the sheet (tab: cost_by_model). Notes from my end:
- Baseline spend: $1.18M/mo (hosted 65%, dedicated 35%) — verified with billing exports through 2026-09.
- Worst-case (20% WoW x6): GPUs required scale ~2.1x peak within 6 weeks; spend projection ~$2.48M/mo if no mitigations.
- Utilization shift: bumping target utilization to 70% via slot consolidation and better packing reduces required GPUs by ~18% in our sim.
- KV cache sensitivity: cache hit delta from 40% -> 60% reduces per-token spend by ~14% in the Samsung-family models (our largest cost center).

I will run a quick simulation of the routing play: route 30% of inference to quantized variants (assume 30% quality delta window for tolerant workloads) and give you projected unit-cost delta and expected impact on latency tail. ETA: tomorrow noon PT.

Attached: qbr_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (updated, tab: scenarios).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Compute Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02 07:15 PDT
Subject: Re: QBR: infra fallback & unit-econ plays (capacity, GPU spend, batching/cache tradeoffs)

Rishi / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of leadership asks to fold into the 6-slide summary:
- Add a single-row SLA-risk matrix that maps each fallback play to: expected SLO impact (none / small / medium / high), confidence level (low/med/high), and recommended communication (customer-facing vs internal).
- Include a concise recommendation for the execs: accept 2 temporary plays (dynamic model-tiering + aggressive KV caching) and avoid broad batch-size increases for real-time routes.
- Prepare a 1-liner 'ask' for Finance: a temporary buffer of $300k runway credit (2 weeks) if the worst-case materializes while we roll out Dedicated nodes.

Marissa — can you slot the Win/Lift estimates into the appendix and flag the ones that require cross-team commitments (runtime, SDK, billing)?

I updated the PDF to call out latency-regression risk for model-tiering; we need a mitigation bullet: A/B canary at 5% traffic with auto-fallback on quality regressions.

I'll review the slide deck draft once you push it to the Drive folder.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procurement@stratuscloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02 09:42 PDT
Subject: Re: QBR: infra fallback & unit-econ plays (capacity, GPU spend, batching/cache tradeoffs)

Rishi —

Appreciate the heads-up. From StratusCloud's side, if Redwood needs to trigger temporary credits for the customers covered under our PS contract, we will need written confirmation of the start/end dates and a rollback plan. Also confirm which customers would be eligible for credits (we need customer identifiers to map to our billing system).

We can turn around an amendment for up to $150k in short-term credits within 48 hours if you provide the customer list and the exact credit logic.

Regards,
Procurement Team
StratusCloud (on behalf of enterprise finance)
